terms.definition: A circuit where each component rides its own branch between two shared rails.
terms.whyItMatters: Sets the rules: full voltage each, independent survival, current splits.
terms.whereItIs: The separate lanes between the top and bottom rails.

terms.definition: Every parallel branch connects straight across the source, so each sees the whole battery volts.
terms.whyItMatters: It's why parallel bulbs shine at full brightness while series ones dim.
terms.whereItIs: The battery feeding both rails at once.

terms.definition: The property that opening one branch leaves every other branch working.
terms.whyItMatters: It's the reason houses are wired parallel so one failure doesn't black out a room.

terms.definition: The point where current splits into the branches and rejoins after them — total equals the sum.
terms.whyItMatters: It explains why the main wire into a parallel set carries more current than any branch.
terms.whereItIs: The meter reading on the rejoin rail.
